design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


Establish exactly what the crate does today before changing anything.

## Already established while filing

- **The stream is package-free by deliberate design.**
  `flowsheet/streams.rs:97-100` records that DWSIM's `AssignSelfToPP` /
  `SetPropertyPackage` / `GetPropertyPackageObject` back-pointer was **not
  ported**; the solver passes a `PropertyPackageModel` explicitly. The
  separation this epic wants is already half-built.
- `MaterialStreamInputData` fields are documented *"at the last solution"* —
  already framed as derived cache.
- `MaterialStreamData.spec: StreamSpec` already records which property pair is
  independent, with `TemperatureAndPressure`, `PressureAndEnthalpy`,
  `PressureAndEntropy`, `PressureAndVaporFraction` variants.

## To determine

- Which quantities should be **canonical** and which **derived/cacheable**.
- Whether `StreamSpec` should be reused as the bridge specification (it maps
  almost exactly onto TP/PH/PS) or whether a separate type is warranted.
- Where units currently obtain their package, and whether that is uniform.
- What `PropertyPackageModel` actually guarantees as a capability surface.

**Do not destroy good existing APIs.** The audit's job is to find the smallest
correct change.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.
title: MultiThermo: Audit current stream / property-package ownership

description:
Efficiency alone pins the WORK but not the MASS FLOW. A digital twin that only holds a design point cannot do sliding-pressure operation, part load, or valve throttling. The missing constitutive law is Stodola's cone (ellipse) law, relating mass flow to inlet and outlet pressure and inlet temperature.

Reference implementation available: ClaRa's 'Steam Turbine L1' (ClaRaLibrary/ClaRa, xrg-simulation/ClaRa-official) is mass + energy conservation with Stodola's law and an isentropic efficiency — structurally the same design as the HemSteamCv-with-sink-terms direction in op-dt3.18. ClaRa official is 3-clause BSD, so GPLv3-compatible one-way and portable WITH its attribution header preserved.

DO NOT port from ThermoPower (casella/ThermoPower): Modelica License 2, not clearly GPL-compatible, does not cleanly permit forking. Read for ideas only.

Maintainer direction 2026-08-04: this lands as a MODULE under tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/ (alongside converging_diverging_nozzles/ and generator.rs), NOT a new crate.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md sections 3.3 and 6.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
ClaRa licence verified directly 2026-08-04 (not from a search summary):

BSD-3-Clause confirmed at THREE levels, all agreeing:
1. Repo LICENSE at xrg-simulation/ClaRa-official — verbatim standard BSD 3-Clause text. Copyright 2013-2023, ClaRa development team = TLK-Thermo GmbH (Braunschweig) + XRG Simulation GmbH (Hamburg).
2. Per-file header on ClaRa/Components/TurboMachines/Turbines/SteamTurbineVLE_L1.mo (v1.9.0): 'Licensed by the ClaRa development team under the 3-clause BSD License. Copyright 2013-2024.' Identical in the ClaRaLibrary/ClaRa mirror.
3. Per-model Documentation annotation in that same file: 'This component was developed by ClaRa development team under the 3-clause BSD License.' Original contribution: DYNCAP/DYNSTART development team, 2011-2024, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (FKZ 03ET2009, FKZ 03ET7060).

FOUR CAVEATS:
- GitHub's licence detector reports NOASSERTION / 'Other' for the repo. FALSE ALARM — caused by the malformed copyright line 'Copyright (c) Copyright 2013-2023,' defeating the strict matcher. Licence body is unmodified BSD-3. Expect automated scans to flag it.
- Use xrg-simulation/ClaRa-official, NOT ClaRaLibrary/ClaRa: the latter has NO LICENSE file at repo root (GitHub API 404), only per-file headers.
- Every ClaRa file warns 'Contents published in ClaRa have been contributed by different authors and institutions. Please see model documentation for detailed information on original authorship and copyrights.' Per-model provenance CAN differ from the blanket licence. SteamTurbineVLE_L1.mo was checked and is clean — do NOT generalise that to other ClaRa models without checking each one.
- ClaRa+ and the older demo distribution are Modelica License 2, NOT BSD. 'ClaRa' is not one thing.

Dependency: the turbine model imports TILMedia functions. The TILMediaClaRa submodule (TLK-Thermo/TILMediaClaRa) is itself BSD-3-Clause, cleanly detected. We do not need it anyway — our property layer is IF97 via TampinesSteamTableCV, so a port takes the Stodola/efficiency/rotor algebra and drops the media calls.

Obligation on porting: retain copyright notice, list of conditions, and disclaimer; do not use the names ClaRa / TLK-Thermo / XRG Simulation to endorse our derived work. Maps onto the workspace attribution header block.

Bonus finding: SteamTurbineVLE_L1.mo already has useMechanicalPort, steadyStateTorque, rpm_fixed and moment of inertia J — i.e. it implements the rotor-inertia coupling this scope calls for in op-dt3.23. Independent confirmation of the design direction.

title: tampines Turbine: Stodola cone (ellipse) law for off-design mass flow vs pressure

description: Found while wiring op-6tz.18 (do NOT fix in this workspace - these are upstream crates). (1) openmc-endf-8-depletion-lib-a/-b: the neutron 'reaction' field on SerdeNuclideData is private, so (n,gamma)/(n,2n) transmutation targets+Q cannot be read from the decay libs; DepletionChain uses hardcoded chain_simple.xml targets instead. Ask upstream to expose the reaction list publicly. (2) fission-yields-data 0.1.4: only u232_thermal_fission_yield is re-exported; u235/u238/... per-nuclide thermal accessors are pub(crate), and fission_yield_linear_interpolation needs a uom-0.37 Energy (this crate is uom 0.38). Ask upstream to re-export per-nuclide thermal accessors (or a by-name f64 lookup) and align uom to 0.38.
title: Upstream data-crate interface gaps for depletion (private reaction targets; non-public fission-yield accessors)

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Engineering model**

**Build after hydrotreating infrastructure works.**

```
pretreated VGO + H2 -> hydrocracker -> HP separator / H2 recycle
                                    -> product fractionator
                                         -> naphtha / jet / diesel
```

Reuse the catalytic kinetics framework, thermo, streams, recycle solver and
separators. **Do not initially attempt thousands of molecular reactions** --
use validated reaction lumps/families.

Depends on hydrotreating, H2 recycle, and the lumping epic.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: Hydrocracking

description:
kovan-discovery, kovan-metrics and kovan-semantics use std::os::unix directly and fail with 'cannot find unix in os'.

Likely candidates: PermissionsExt (file modes), OsStrExt, CommandExt, or symlink handling in the fd/ripgrep walker.

Fix: cfg-gate the unix-specific code and provide a portable fallback, OR gate the whole capability off wasm where it makes no sense. Worth asking per site which it is — a file-permission check has no meaning in a browser, whereas a path-to-bytes conversion does and should use the portable API.

NOTE the honest question behind this one: kovan is a local-first developer CLI/TUI that walks the filesystem and shells out to language servers. kovan itself already shows 36 files using std::fs. 'Compiles for wasm' is therefore close to meaningless for these three crates in isolation — nothing about them would FUNCTION in a browser.

So decide explicitly, and record the decision:
  (a) make them compile for wasm anyway, for uniformity and to keep the CI gate simple; or
  (b) declare them out of scope, exclude them from the gate with a stated reason.
Option (b) is defensible and may be the honest answer. What is NOT acceptable is quietly making them compile and letting a future reader infer they work.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
CANCELLED — EXCLUDED by maintainer decision, 2026-09-04: the kovan crates are out of scope for wasm.

This bead put the question rather than assuming, and option (b) — 'declare them out of scope with a stated reason' — is the answer. kovan is a local-first developer CLI/TUI that walks the filesystem and shells out to language servers; kovan itself has 36 files using std::fs. 'Compiles for wasm' would have been close to meaningless for kovan-discovery / kovan-metrics / kovan-semantics.

Excluded from the class-F gate: kovan, kovan-discovery, kovan-metrics, kovan-semantics — the four that fail.

DELIBERATELY NOT EXCLUDED: kovan-codegen, kovan-common and kovan-literature already PASS the wasm check today. Keeping them in the gate costs nothing and protects the pure-data half of the kovan layer from regressing. They are the parts a browser could plausibly use (canonical types, literature records), unlike the filesystem walker and the language-server bridge. If the whole family should come out, that is a one-line change to the exclusion list — but an exclusion should be as narrow as its reason supports.

title: wasm class D: std::os::unix in three kovan crates
